gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured power or noise figure for any NAS it recommended. ComputerBase measured the DXP2800 at the same 18.6 W idle as the J4125 Synology DS224+, with spun-down standby at 7.3 W vs 3.5 W. PCWorld measured the QNAP TS-264 at 26.5 W idle and LinuxLinks measured the Asustor AS5402T at 29.2 W, so either costs about 8–11 W more to run 24/7 as a music server.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited and those at the top of its results. Navidrome Overview (navidrome.org/docs/overview) only says Navidrome runs on modest hardware. UGREEN's Navidrome Docker guide (ai.ugreen.com) covers setup and has no measurements. Plex's Sonic Analysis page returned 403 to me; its search snippet says only that analysis takes 'hours or even multiple days' depending on the CPU. Plex's Media Server Requirements page has general CPU guidance only. ChatGPT's answers asked for 'low idle power' and 'quiet operation' but gave no watt or dB figure for the DXP2800, DS225+, TS-264 or AS5402T. None of these pages has a measured idle draw, noise level or Sonic Analysis speed.
decides: This backs the DXP2800 over the TS-264 and AS5402T for an always-on FLAC server. ComputerBase measured the DXP2800 at the same idle draw as Synology's J4125 platform and quieter at idle. The TS-264 and AS5402T idled 8–11 W higher in their reviewers' tests, roughly 69–93 kWh a year more. Those come from different labs with different drives. The DS224+/DS225+ spins down to less than half the DXP2800's standby draw (3.5 W vs 7.3 W), which helps a library that is played only a few hours a day. The power figures don't separate the DXP2800 from the Synology. The tiebreak is CPU, since Sonic Analysis is CPU-bound and the N100 is newer and faster than the J4125. I have no side-by-side measurement of the CPU gap: Notebookcheck's J4125 vs N100 page returned 403.

A measured dB(A) figure for the QNAP TS-264 and AS5402T: PCWorld rates noise only in words, and LinuxLinks didn't measure it. The 18.6 dB figures that turned up are spec-sheet values.
Igor'sLab DXP2800 power/noise page (igorslab.de/en/ugreen-nasync-dxp2800-nas-im-test/8) returned 403, so I couldn't open it.

Notebookcheck's measured CPU comparison of the Celeron J4125 vs N100 (notebookcheck.net/Celeron-J4125-vs-N100...) returned 403, so I have no side-by-side measurement of how much faster the N100 is for Sonic Analysis.

Trusted Reviews' DS225+ power figure (a 13 W peak, May 2026) and NASCompares' ~10 W idle figure appeared only on aggregator pages. The NASCompares review I opened restates Synology's spec figures (16.98 W access, 6.08 W hibernation) and gives 19.6 dB(A) idle with no stated method.
A measured Sonic Analysis speed on a J4125 Synology (DS224+/DS225+) or on the DXP2800 itself: Plex forum threads give no timing tied to a named model.
Measurements for the Raspberry Pi 5 and Mac mini M4 rows: not researched within the tool budget.
